## Summary

## Summary

Fixes #128 — problem **2** (the guard's placement). An orphan tag (`v0.56.0`) made `scripts/check-github-releases.rs` fail *after* the new release had already been created, so `Create GitHub Release` failed and every Docker job was skipped: v0.57.0 and v0.58.0 got releases but no images.

## Root cause

`Verify GitHub Releases` ran as the last step of `create-github-release`, checking the **whole tag history** and hard-failing. A pre-existing orphan is unrelated to the version being published, but it blocked it — and blocked it after the release existed, producing exactly the state the guard is meant to prevent.

## Changes

- `scripts/check-github-releases.rs`
  - `--release-version <v>` scopes the hard failure to the tag being published right now.
  - `--historical-orphans warn|error` (default `error`) — earlier orphans can be reported without failing.
  - Error/warning text now names the remediation for each orphan tag.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
  - New `Report pre-existing release drift` step runs **before** the release is created (warn mode), so drift shows up in the log while it can still be fixed cleanly.
  - `Verify GitHub Releases` now runs with `--release-version "${{ env.RELEASE_VERSION }}" --historical-orphans warn`, so it only fails if *this* run's release is missing — Docker jobs are no longer blocked by unrelated history.
- `.github/workflows/verify-releases.yml` unchanged: the scheduled reconciliation still fails hard on any default-branch tag without a release. That's the right place to enforce history.

## Reproduction and verification

Against the live repository (v0.56.0 is still orphaned):

```
$ rust-script scripts/check-github-releases.rs --repository link-assistant/router --default-branch main
Error: pre-existing tags without a GitHub Release:
v0.56.0
Resolve each orphan tag by either creating the missing release
  gh release create v0.56.0 --title v0.56.0 --notes-from-tag
or deleting the tag if that version was never meant to ship
  git push origin :refs/tags/v0.56.0
exit=1                      # old behaviour — this is what killed the Docker jobs

$ rust-script scripts/check-github-releases.rs --repository link-assistant/router \
    --default-branch main --release-version 0.58.0 --historical-orphans warn
Warning: pre-existing tags without a GitHub Release:
v0.56.0
...
exit=0                      # release run proceeds; images publish
```

## Tests

- `scripts/check-github-releases.rs`: `scopes_the_current_release_apart_from_earlier_orphans`, `treats_every_orphan_as_historical_without_a_release_version`, `remediation_names_both_ways_out_for_the_reported_tag` (run in CI via `rust-script --test`).
- `tests/release_workflow_test.rs`: new `historical_orphan_tags_do_not_block_the_current_release` asserts the drift report precedes release creation, that it warns rather than fails, and that the post-release check is version-scoped; `release_workflows_detect_missing_github_releases` updated to require the scoped guard in the release run and the unscoped hard guard in the scheduled workflow.

`cargo test --test release_workflow_test`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` all pass locally.

## Still to do by a human (problem 1 in the issue)

The orphan tag `v0.56.0` itself is a repository-state fix, not a code fix, and is left to a maintainer:

- create the missing release: `gh release create v0.56.0 --title v0.56.0 --notes-from-tag`, or
- delete the tag if 0.56.0 was never meant to ship: `git push origin :refs/tags/v0.56.0`

With this PR merged, releases are unblocked either way. Re-running the release for 0.57.0/0.58.0 (or cutting 0.59.0) is what actually publishes the missing images.
title: fix(ci): scope the release guard to the version being published

Closes #50.

A minimal admin console, built on **Chakra UI v3** (Horizon UI as a visual reference only — not a v2 fork), embedded in the binary and served by the router on a **separate listener that does not exist unless you give it a port**.

```bash
link-assistant-router --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --admin-host 127.0.0.1 --admin-port 8081
```

| Flag / env | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--admin-port` / `ADMIN_PORT` | — (disabled) | Port for the admin listener. No port, no admin surface at all. |
| `--admin-host` / `ADMIN_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Address the admin listener binds, independent of the proxy. |
| `--admin-claim-ttl-secs` / `ADMIN_CLAIM_TTL_SECS` | `120` | Lifetime of an unconfirmed bootstrap candidate. |

## Who is the administrator

Either `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` decides at deploy time, or the first browser to arrive claims the router — through a **two-phase** handshake, because the obvious one-phase version bricks the deployment when the response is lost (closed laptop, dropped connection, a browser that refuses `localStorage`): nobody holds the credential, and bootstrap is already closed.

| Step | Request | Effect on the server |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `POST /api/admin/bootstrap` | Mints a candidate token and a `claim_id`. **Nothing is persisted. The candidate authorises nothing. The system is still unclaimed.** |
| 2 | *(browser)* | Writes the token to `localStorage` and **reads it back** |
| 3 | `POST /api/admin/bootstrap/confirm` with `{claim_id}`, authenticated with that freshly stored token | Activates the credential and closes bootstrap |

Only step 3 changes anything durable, so:

- an unconfirmed candidate expires after the TTL and leaves the system **unclaimed** — a lost mint is always retryable;
- only one candidate is outstanding at a time, so the first to **confirm** wins and the loser's candidate is discarded;
- when the read-back in step 2 fails the client deliberately **does not confirm** — it shows the token for manual copy and leaves bootstrap open.

Only the SHA-256 digest of the active credential is persisted (`<data-dir>/admin-claim.json`); the token itself is never stored server-side and never re-displayed. **Rotate credential** mints a replacement and retires the old one in one step (disabled when `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` is set).

## What the UI does

Tokens: list (id, label, issued, expires, used/max requests, revoked), issue (label, TTL, optional request cap, optional account pin) with the value shown **once**, revoke behind a confirmation dialog. Status: read-only version, upstream, credential state, `/v1/accounts`, `/v1/usage`. `doctor` now prints `admin_ui` and `admin_credential`.

| The claim screen | Issuing a token |
| --- | --- |

## The trade-off, documented

The admin token lives in the browser's `localStorage` — that is what lets the client *prove* it stored the credential before the server commits. `docs/use-cases/admin-ui.md` spells out the consequences: any script on the admin origin can read it, it survives restarts until sign-out or rotation, and a shared machine is a shared admin credential. - Local: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (clean, no new warnings), full `cargo test`.

## Notes

- `ui/dist` is committed and embedded with `rust-embed`, so CI needs no Node toolchain; `ui/node_modules` is gitignored.

The existing workflow ran `cargo test` across three operating systems but never instrumented production code, recorded a baseline, or placed coverage in the build/release dependency graph. Before this change, the focused workflow regression test failed because no coverage job or behavioral checker existed.

The canonical Ubuntu CI run measured **14,884 / 19,374 lines = 76.824610%**. A local run covered 18 additional lines, so the enforcing runner is the source of truth. Because that is below the requested 80% target, enforcing 80% immediately would deadlock all pull requests. This PR starts the ratchet at the measured value and documents four coverage-focused milestones: 77.50%, 78.50%, 79.25%, and 80.00%. Once the baseline reaches 80%, the permanent absolute floor remains 80% while the ratchet can continue above it.

## Coverage policy

`cargo-llvm-cov` uses its stable default exclusions: dependencies, vendored sources, `tests/`, `tests.rs`, and `*_tests.rs` files are excluded. Inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules in production files remain part of the file-level report because excluding them requires unstable coverage attributes. The exact policy, local commands, ramp, escape hatch, and caveat that line coverage is not evidence of correctness are documented in `docs/test-coverage.md`.

## Automated tests

- workflow regression test: coverage runs exactly once on `ubuntu-latest`, cleans stale profiles, fails closed, emits a job summary, and gates the build
- checker unit tests: absolute 80% floor, below-target ramp, ratchet above the floor, default-branch anti-tampering check, automatic baseline file update, and labelled exception
- pre-fix regression evidence: `cargo test --locked --test release_workflow_test coverage_` failed before the implementation

## Summary

- persist the native Claude OAuth PKCE verifier and state in the Claude config directory for 15 minutes
- resume and atomically consume that transaction when `auth claude --flow code --code ...` runs in a later process or container
- reject incompatible `--flow cli --code` input without starting an unrelated login
- document the two-step remote/container workflow and add a patch changelog fragment

## Root cause

The native code flow always called `LoginManager::begin`, including invocations that already supplied `--code`. That generated a new state and PKCE verifier, so a code returned for the earlier authorization URL could never pass state validation in the later process.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

The updated Claude auth integration test begins a persisted login, drops the original login object to simulate process exit, resumes it, and verifies the token exchange uses the original state and verifier. New CLI black-box tests verify that a supplied code never prints a fresh authorization URL and that incompatible CLI fallback input is rejected.

Closes #49.

## The problem

`is_admin_authorised` in `src/proxy.rs` did two things wrong:

1. It compared `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` with `==` — a flat, short-circuiting secret with no identity, expiry, scope, revocation or rotation.
2. When `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` was unset it returned `true`, so `/api/tokens*` was **unauthenticated by default**.

Reproduction (before this PR): start the router with no `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` and `POST /api/tokens` with no `Authorization` header → `200` plus a usable `la_sk_…` token.

## The fix

Admin access is now a **scoped JWT on the existing `TokenManager` path**, so it inherits expiry, revocation, identity and rotation:

- `TokenClaims`/`TokenRecord` carry a `scope`; `ADMIN_SCOPE = "admin"`. Client tokens carry no scope and are rejected on the admin surface.
- `TokenManager::issue_admin_token`, `validate_admin_token`, `has_active_admin_token`, `rotate_admin_token` (issue replacement + revoke the old `sub` in one step; an unknown id is an error, not a silent no-op).
- `tokens issue --admin`, new `tokens rotate <id>`, a `scope` column in `tokens list`, and `POST /api/tokens {"scope":"admin"}` / `POST /api/tokens/rotate` over HTTP. An unknown scope is a `400`.
- The flat `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` keeps working unchanged as a bootstrap credential, now compared in constant time (SHA-256 both sides, XOR fold — the crate forbids `unsafe_code`).

**The default is closed**, implementing both options the issue listed:

- On first start with no credential configured, the router mints an admin token, prints it once, and persists only its record — admin endpoints stay closed.
- Anonymous admin access now requires an explicit opt-out: `--allow-anonymous-admin` / `ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ADMIN=1`. `doctor` reports `admin_endpoints : OPEN (--allow-anonymous-admin)` when it is set.

The decision itself lives in a new `src/admin_auth.rs` as a pure function over `(manager, provided, admin_key, allow_anonymous)`, so it is testable without an `AppState`; `proxy.rs` is a thin wrapper over it.

## Tests

- `src/admin_auth.rs` — 8 unit tests pinning the rule, including the issue's reproduction (`unauthenticated_request_is_refused_when_no_credential_is_configured`), revoked/expired admin tokens, client-token rejection, and the flat-key path.
- `tests/admin_endpoints_test.rs` (new, unix) — 8 end-to-end tests that boot the real binary on a loopback port and speak HTTP: anonymous `POST /api/tokens` → `401`, the bootstrap token is printed and works, client tokens are refused, admin tokens are issuable and rotatable, unknown scope → `400`, the flat key still authorises, and `ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ADMIN=1` restores the old open surface.
- `src/token.rs` / `src/storage.rs` — scope round-trips through the text and binary stores; rotation issues a replacement, revokes the old id, and rejects an unknown subject.
- `experiments/issue-45/test-deployment-hardening.sh` — rewritten to assert the closed default against a container: **18 passed, 0 failed** (was 16, and it previously asserted the open behaviour).

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (clean), and the file-size budget all pass. Full suite: 279 passed.

## Notes

- No `Cargo.toml` version bump — manual bumps are blocked by the `version-check` job; `changelog.d/20260807_190000_issue_49_scoped_admin_tokens.md` carries `bump: minor`.
- `tests/release_workflow_test.rs::dockerfile_offers_a_claude_cli_variant_without_bloating_the_default_image` was failing here **and on a clean `main`**: issue #47's PR duplicated the `nodejs` + `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` install into the `runtime-base` stage that issue #48's test asserts stays minimal — the identical install already exists in the `with-claude-cli` stage layered directly on top, so every default `docker build .` shipped the CLI twice over and `:latest` stopped being the minimal image. Fixed here (`fe23013`) by dropping it from the base stage and pointing `docs/use-cases/remote-login.md` at the `with-claude-cli` variant, since CI stays red otherwise.

Fixes #85.

## 1. `/v1/responses` rejects a string `input`

**Reproduce**

```bash
curl -s localhost:8787/v1/responses -H 'authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-sol","input":"скажи ок"}'
# {"detail":"Input must be a list"}   HTTP 400
```

**Root cause** — `normalize_codex_responses_body` (`src/subscription_proxy.rs`) only ever
manipulated `input` when it was already a `Value::Array` (to hoist system/developer turns into
`instructions`). A `Value::String` fell straight through to the ChatGPT backend, which accepts
only the list form. The Responses API documents both.

**Fix** — `responses::normalize_input_items` converts a bare string (and any bare string inside
the list) into the typed single user turn `{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":…}]}`,
leaving already-typed items untouched. It runs before the system-turn hoisting.

**Tests** — `responses::tests::normalizes_string_input_and_preserves_typed_input` and
`subscription_proxy::tests::codex_normalizes_both_documented_input_forms_to_a_list`, which asserts
the string form, the already-typed list form and `["скажи ок"]` all leave the router as the same
list. #70 was the mirror image of this gap, so both forms are now pinned.

## 2. `expiresAt` treated as a verdict while the credential still works

**Reproduce** — a Claude credential stamped expired is dropped by `GET /v1/models` (401) although
`/v1/messages` still returns a real completion with real usage.

**Root cause** — `model_routing::healthy_providers` returned `(!token.is_expired(now_ms)).then_some(provider)`,
and `model_catalog::refresh_catalogs` short-circuited with `credential is expired and could not be
refreshed` without ever contacting the vendor. A timestamp alone removed a working provider.

**Fix** — `expiresAt` is now a hint:

- `TokenCache` records `CredentialEvidence` (`Working`/`Rejected`) from real upstream statuses;
  both inference forwarders report it (`proxy.rs` Anthropic path, `subscription_proxy.rs`
  OpenAI-shaped path).
- A stamped-expired provider stays routable until an upstream 401/403 is actually observed.
- Catalog refresh is attempted with the stamped-expired token; on failure the last known models
  are kept (`using_fallback`) and the error says why.
- `doctor` distinguishes `EXPIRED on disk but ACCEPTED upstream` from `EXPIRED and REJECTED`, and
  surfaces `invalid_grant` as "re-authenticate this subscription; waiting will not help".

**Tests** — `model_routing::tests::expired_credential_stays_routable_without_an_upstream_rejection`,
`model_catalog::tests::expired_credential_is_still_probed_and_keeps_its_cached_catalog` (stub
upstream answering 401), and three `refresh::tests` covering evidence recording and the
`invalid_grant` message.

## Checks

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (clean), `cargo test` — 425 tests,
0 failures. `src/proxy.rs` stays at the 1000-line project limit. A `changelog.d` fragment
(`bump: patch`) is included to trigger the release.
title: fix: normalise string Responses input and treat expiresAt as a hint

Closes #51.

Adds two **optional** chat channels that administer the router from a private conversation. The web UI stays the default and only channel out of the box: nothing here runs unless a bot token is configured, and each channel is independent.

> [!NOTE]
> Built on top of #56 (the web admin UI and the shared `AdminClaim`), which is merged into this branch. Review the diff after that merge, or merge #56 first.

## What it does

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `/start` → `/confirm <token>` | Claim administration (two-phase, only while unclaimed) |
| `/auth <token>` / `/logout` | Bind / forget an admin credential for this conversation |
| `/status` | Read-only: credential state, upstream, account health, usage |
| `/tokens` | id, label, expiry, usage, revoked — **never a token value** |
| `/issue <label> [ttl_hours] [max_requests]` | Issue a token (sent once, in its own message) |
| `/revoke <id>` | Revoke a token |
| `/rotate` | Replace the admin credential, in every channel at once |

## One system-wide claim

The bots hold the *same* `AdminClaim` as the web UI, so a deployment has one first admin, not one per channel:

- a claim confirmed in a browser closes `/start` in chat, and a claim confirmed in chat closes `POST /api/admin/bootstrap` (409);
- `/start` mints a candidate that authorises nothing and persists nothing — only `/confirm` (or sending the token back bare) activates it, so a message that never arrived cannot brick administration;
- a deployment with `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` starts already claimed and `/start` refuses;
- after the claim, every other chat user must present a valid admin credential. The platform user id is only a **cache** for it: every command re-validates, so revoking or rotating signs the chat user out on their next message. `--allow-anonymous-admin` does not open a chat channel.

## Secrets and hostile input

- **Private chats only.** Telegram requires `chat.type == "private"` (bot senders and senderless messages are dropped too); VK requires `peer_id == from_id`, positive, below the `2000000000` multi-user chat offset. Group traffic never reaches the command parser.
- Credentials are sent in their own message and deleted after `--chat-admin-secret-ttl-secs` (default 120), and the message says so.
- Listings never echo a token value.
- `/start`, `/auth`, `/confirm`, `/issue`, `/rotate` are rate limited per user (default 5/min).

## Configuration

| Flag / env | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `--telegram-bot-token` / `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | — (channel off) |
| `--vk-bot-token` / `VK_BOT_TOKEN` (+ `--vk-group-id` / `VK_GROUP_ID`) | — (channel off) |
| `--chat-admin-secret-ttl-secs` / `CHAT_ADMIN_SECRET_TTL_SECS` | `120` |
| `--chat-admin-rate-limit-per-minute` / `CHAT_ADMIN_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `5` |

`doctor` reports `telegram_admin_bot` and `vk_admin_bot`.

## Implementation

Rust in-process, no bot framework — plain `reqwest` against the documented HTTP APIs, long polling rather than webhooks so the deployment needs no public surface.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/chat_admin.rs` | Transport-agnostic core: claim sharing, sessions, authorisation, rate limiting |
| `src/chat_commands.rs` | What the authorised commands do; `RouterStatus` trait keeps the core free of `AppState` |
| `src/telegram.rs`, `src/vk.rs` | Thin polling loops: private-chat filtering, send, delayed delete |
| `src/chat_config.rs` | Flags and environment variables |

## Tests

- Unit tests in each new module (48 tests): claim sharing both directions, unconfirmed mints leaving the router claimable, second-user authorisation, JWT accepted / client token rejected, revocation unbinding a chat user, sessions not leaking across channels or users, rate limiting, `@botname` command suffixes, private-chat filtering for both platforms, and that listings never carry a value.
- `tests/chat_admin_test.rs` drives the real admin HTTP router and the chat core against one on-disk claim: a web-UI claim closes `/start`, a chat claim returns `409` from the browser bootstrap, a token issued from chat validates against the router and is gone after `/revoke`, and group traffic is filtered.

`cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (pedantic + nursery) are clean.

## Docs

New [docs/use-cases/chat-admin-bots.md](docs/use-cases/chat-admin-bots.md), linked from the use-case index, plus a README section for the surface and its settings. Changelog fragment `changelog.d/20260807_chat_admin_channels.md` (`bump: minor`).

body:
Closes #47.

A Docker deployment could previously only be authorized by mounting a credential file that was produced somewhere else. There was no way to log in *to the deployment*. This adds one.

## The API

| Request | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/login` | Starts the Claude Code CLI on a real PTY **inside the deployment** and returns the authorization URL it printed |
| *(human)* | Opens the URL, approves, copies the code |
| `POST /api/login/{id}/code` | Types that code into the **same, still-running** process |
| `GET /api/login/{id}` | `awaiting_code` \| `authorized` \| `failed` \| `expired` |
| `DELETE /api/login/{id}` | Cancels a pending login and kills its process |

```console
$ curl -sX POST localhost:8080/api/login -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
{"login_id":"3f2b…","status":"awaiting_code","url":"https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize?…", …}

$ curl -sX POST localhost:8080/api/login/3f2b…/code -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"code":"abc123#xyz"}'
{"login_id":"3f2b…","status":"authorized","expires_at":1786500000000, …}
```

## The part that's easy to get wrong

The human step in the middle takes minutes, so **the process started by the first request must outlive it**. It does: sessions live in a registry keyed by `login_id` holding the live child, its PTY and its terminal state, and the code-submitting request writes into the PTY the first request created. Everything the issue's comments asked for follows from that:

- **Separate, generous TTL** with an explicit `expired` status (`--login-session-ttl-secs`, default 900s), distinct from `failed` — "start over" vs "the code was wrong".
- **Bounded concurrency** (`--login-max-sessions`, default 4); beyond the cap `POST /api/login` is `429`.
- **Explicit cleanup on every terminal path** — success, failure, `DELETE`, and TTL expiry all kill the child and free the slot.

## Design notes

- **No `unsafe`.** The crate is `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, so the PTY comes from `portable-pty` rather than hand-rolled `forkpty`.
- **Reading a TUI is not `read_to_string`.** `login_pty.rs` waits for a predicate that holds *and* has been quiet for an idle interval, so it never parses a half-painted frame; `login_url.rs` undoes terminal hard-wrapping and takes the **last** URL match, because a TUI repaints the same URL many times.
- **The outcome is decided by the filesystem, not by log scraping.** After the code is submitted the flow probes the credential file; only if there is none does it fall back to extracting the `sk-ant-…` token from the transcript and writing it in the nested `claudeAiOauth` layout `OAuthProvider` reads. Success markers are a hint, never the verdict.
- **It takes effect without a restart.** The proxy caches the token it read at boot, so a successful login calls `oauth_provider.refresh_token()`.
- **It fails early, not late.** `CLAUDE_CODE_HOME` is write-probed *before* the URL is returned, so a read-only mount errors immediately instead of after the human has already finished in the browser.
- **These are admin endpoints** (`TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY`), consistent with `/api/tokens/list`, and `--disable-login-api` removes the routes entirely.

`command-stream`'s `captureTerminal()` was the semantic reference for the PTY handling, but its lifecycle (one batch, 30s then SIGTERM, resolves only after the child exits) is exactly what does not fit here, so only the semantics were borrowed.

## How to reproduce and verify

`tests/login_flow_test.rs` (**7 passed**) drives the whole flow against `examples/fake-login-cli.sh` — a stand-in for `claude setup-token` that repaints like the real TUI, waits on stdin, and prints an `sk-ant-oat…` token. It asserts:

- the URL is recovered from the repainting TUI;
- a **separate later call** reaches the same live process and authorizes it;
- the resulting credential is readable by `OAuthProvider`, the component that actually serves upstream requests — not merely present on disk;
- a rejected code fails the session and leaves **no** credential behind;
- a code cannot be submitted twice, cancelling frees the slot, expiry reports `expired` and stops accepting codes, and the concurrency cap returns an error.

Plus unit tests for ANSI/OSC stripping, key encoding, wrap-rejoining, repaint handling and credential writing. Full suite: **256 passed, 0 failed**; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` and the 1000-line file-size check are clean.

## Also in this PR

- The image ships the Claude Code CLI and Node — without them the flow has nothing to drive — and pre-creates the writable `/data/claude`.
- `docs/use-cases/remote-login.md`, linked from the use-case index and the README endpoint/flag tables.
- A changelog fragment. The version is intentionally **not** bumped: `scripts/check-version-modification.rs` fails PRs that touch it, and release automation derives the bump from `changelog.d/`.

## One known limitation, pinned by a test

A URL that ends *exactly* on a terminal wrap boundary is genuinely ambiguous — its final screen line is full, so nothing distinguishes "the terminal wrapped" from "the program ended the line", and the next line's text gets glued on. `a_url_ending_exactly_on_the_boundary_absorbs_the_next_line` pins this rather than hiding it. It is harmless in practice because `PTY_COLS` is 400, far wider than any URL Claude prints, so no wrap occurs at all.

## What this PR does

Extends multi-account routing from Claude-only pools to every subscription provider already supported by the router: Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Qwen. It also adds stable session assignment, strict token account pins, internal request caps, quota-aware selection/cooldowns, and Formal AI-style native protocol namespaces.

## Root cause and reproduction

PR #38 added vendor credential readers and single-subscription forwarding, but `AccountRouter` still constructed Claude-only `OAuthProvider` instances. Codex, Gemini, and Qwen therefore bypassed account selection; refreshed credentials were cached only by provider; and OpenAI translation discarded session metadata before selection.

The regression tests added first reproduced those gaps as 26 missing API/type errors, including provider-neutral pool construction, strict session/pin selection, per-account refresh keys, request caps, and request-routing context extraction.

- One provider-neutral pool backed by `SubscriptionReader` for Claude, Codex, Gemini, or Qwen.

Closes #52.

A deliberate security review pass over the surface added by #47 (login API on a PTY), #49 (scoped admin JWTs), #50 (admin console + bootstrap claim) and #51 (Telegram/VK admin bots) — run as a defined pass, with the whole pass **written down, including what was found to be fine**, in [`docs/security/review-2026-08.md`](docs/security/review-2026-08.md).

## Threat model (written down explicitly)

The router holds a credential to a **paid** account, so compromise costs money directly. The realistic adversary is anyone who can reach an exposed port — including someone who finds the deployment *before its owner completes the first-run claim*. The full table, plus what is deliberately out of scope, is in the document.

## Findings fixed (4), each with a regression test

| | Finding | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **F1** | The admin listener sent no security headers, while its client keeps the credential in `localStorage` and its revoke/rotate actions are one click — no containment for injected script, and the console was framable. | `src/security_headers.rs`, applied as the **outermost** layer so it also covers UI assets and the auth middleware's own refusals: `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `script-src 'self'`, `form-action 'none'`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. |
| **F2** | `SUCCESS_MARKERS` contains `"sk-ant-oat"` — proof the paid-account credential appears in the PTY transcript — and that transcript's tail was quoted verbatim into login API error strings. A login failing *after* the token printed handed it to the caller. | `login_url::redact_secrets` + `redact_value`, applied **before** truncation so a length limit cannot leave a usable prefix. The pasted authorization code is removed too. |
| **F3** | `LoginManager` never evicted terminal sessions; `ChatAdmin.sessions` was keyed by an *unauthenticated* platform user id and never evicted anyone. | Login: `settled_at` + 300 s retention, and expiry drops the PTY (killing the child). Chat: pruned every message, 1 h idle TTL, 512-entry cap evicting credential-less strangers first, never the current conversation. |
| **F4** | `ENABLE_METRICS` defaults to `true` (`src/config.rs:346`), mounting `/v1/usage` (token ids, labels) and `/v1/accounts` (credential filesystem paths) unauthenticated on the **network-facing** proxy port. | Both now require `is_admin_authorised`. `/metrics` stays open on purpose — aggregate counters only. |

## How to reproduce / verify

Each finding has an automated test that fails without its fix:

- `tests/security_review_test.rs` — `every_admin_response_is_hardened` (F1), `the_disclosing_read_endpoints_require_admin_but_metrics_stays_scrapable` (F4), plus the two checklist properties the issue asked to pin: `the_bootstrap_claim_can_be_won_only_once_across_channels` (wins the claim *in chat*, then asserts HTTP `/api/admin/bootstrap` returns 409 and a second chat user is handed nothing) and `a_client_token_is_refused_where_an_admin_credential_is_required` (both ports).
- `src/login_url.rs` — `a_printed_credential_never_survives_redaction`, `the_routers_own_credentials_are_redacted_whole` (F2).
- `src/login.rs` — `a_failure_excerpt_carries_neither_the_token_nor_the_pasted_code`, `finished_sessions_are_evicted_once_their_result_has_been_retained`, `an_expired_session_becomes_evictable` (F2, F3).
- `src/chat_admin.rs` — `a_flood_of_strangers_cannot_grow_the_session_map_without_bound`, `the_active_conversation_survives_the_cap` (F3).

`cargo test --all-features`: **all green** (275 lib tests + integration suites, 0 failures). `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean.

## Checked and found fine (recorded, not silently dropped)

Restart between mint and confirm discards the candidate and leaves the system unclaimed (fails towards claimable, never towards silently claimed); a minted candidate authorises nothing; only the SHA-256 digest is persisted; `require_admin` is a router-wide middleware with an explicit three-entry allow-list, so new routes are protected by default; comparisons are constant-time and length-safe; chat credentials are re-validated on **every** command, so revocation and rotation take effect immediately; `login_id` is a v4 UUID; Telegram requests `allowed_updates: ["message"]` so edited messages never arrive, and VK enforces `peer_id == from_id`; CSRF is inapplicable (Bearer header, no cookie, no CORS layer installed); no `trace!`/`debug!` site logs a token, header or key, the audit log records `token_id` not the token, and `doctor` prints credential *states*, never values.

Residual accepted risks (first-run claim window, `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` required by emotion, `localStorage` storage, candidate tokens in chat history, `--data-dir` write access resetting the claim) are enumerated in the document rather than left implicit.

## CI

New `Dependency Audit` job: `cargo audit` plus `npm audit --audit-level=high` for the `ui/` JS toolchain. It deliberately does **not** gate `build` — an advisory can be published against an unchanged tree, and that should raise a red check, not block an unrelated release.

## Summary

Fixes #35.

This PR uses the local Docker + Claude MAX access to run the router end-to-end,
verifies that everything the docs claim actually works, fixes the one genuine
code bug found, and adds the "limit how much each task can use" capability the
issue asks for.

Three outcomes:

1. **Fixed the real root-cause bug.** Real Claude Code writes its OAuth session
   to `~/.claude/.credentials.json` nested under a `claudeAiOauth` object. The
   router only read a *flat* `accessToken`, so against an actual login it found
   no token. `src/oauth.rs` now reads both the nested and flat layouts.
2. **Proved token hiding + transparent passthrough** end-to-end against
   `api.anthropic.com`, both natively and through the Docker image. A client
   sending only a `la_sk_` token (no `anthropic-version`, no OAuth beta header)
   gets a working upstream response; the real OAuth token never appears in logs
   or client-visible output.
3. **Added a per-token request budget** so a scoped token can be handed to a
   separate task with a hard cap on how many upstream requests it may make.

## Changes

### Fixed — nested Claude MAX credential layout (`src/oauth.rs`)
- `extract_token()` / `expires_at_ms()` accept both the nested `claudeAiOauth`
  object (real Claude Code) and the flat `{"accessToken": ...}` layout.
- `doctor` probes the credential file and reports `found, token OK` /
  `found, NO TOKEN` / `MISSING`.

### Added — per-token request budget (`max_requests`)
- `src/storage.rs`: `TokenRecord` gains `max_requests: Option<u64>` and
  `used_requests: u64` (both `#[serde(default)]`, backward compatible); the Lino
  text codec round-trips `(max_requests N)` / `(used_requests N)`;
  `TokenStore::try_consume_request` checks-and-increments.
- `src/token.rs`: `issue_token_full(...)` writes the cap;
  `enforce_request_budget(...)` returns `TokenError::LimitExceeded` once hit.
- `src/proxy.rs`: every forwarding path (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gonka) enforces the
  budget after token validation and returns `429 rate_limit_error` when
  exhausted. Admin token endpoints were extracted to a new `src/token_admin.rs`
  to stay under the 1000-line per-file CI limit.
- `src/cli.rs` / `src/main.rs` / `src/token_admin.rs`: `tokens issue
  --max-requests`, the `POST /api/tokens` `max_requests` field, and a `used/max`
  column in `tokens list`.

### Docs
- README: documented the nested credential layout, transparent header injection
  (`anthropic-version` default + `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20`), and the
  per-token budget; corrected the stale note claiming revocations are lost on
  restart (records are persisted).
- `docs/case-studies/issue-35/`: full case study — requirement-by-requirement
  trace, online research (primary sources), existing-components survey (LiteLLM
  virtual keys/budgets, Portkey, Kong AI Gateway, community Claude proxies), and
  redacted live + Docker evidence.
- `changelog.d/20260609_233000_issue_35_local_testing.md` (`bump: minor`).

## How it was verified (live + Docker)

Performed against `https://api.anthropic.com` with a **copy** of the real Claude
MAX credentials. The original `~/.claude/.credentials.json` was only read/copied
— never modified or deleted (confirmed unchanged at 471 bytes).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Client sends only `la_sk_` token to `count_tokens` | HTTP 200 `{"input_tokens":13}` |
| Real OAuth token in server / container logs | 0 occurrences |
| Missing token | 401 |
| Invalid token | 401 |
| Revoked token | 403 |
| Capped token after its budget | our 429 `Token has reached its request limit` (no upstream `request_id`) |
| Usage persistence | text store `(max_requests 2) (used_requests 2)`; `tokens list` → `2/2` |
| Docker image (`Dockerfile`) with copied creds mounted `:ro` | identical results; nested creds read; no token leak |

Evidence: `docs/case-studies/issue-35/raw/` (native) and
`docs/case-studies/issue-35/raw/docker/` (container).

> Note: live `/v1/messages` inference returned an upstream `429` with a genuine
> Anthropic `request_id` — a real account-level inference rate limit on the
> shared MAX account, not a router bug. `count_tokens` (not inference-metered)
> returning 200 through the same path proves the proxy path itself is healthy.

## Tests

- New unit tests in `src/token.rs`: `test_unlimited_token_never_hits_budget`,
  `test_request_budget_enforced` (caps at 3, 4th = `LimitExceeded`, usage
  persisted), `test_budget_for_unknown_token_is_permitted`.
- `src/storage.rs` round-trip literals updated for the new fields.
- `src/oauth.rs` tests cover nested + flat layouts.

## Local CI gate (all green)

`cargo fmt --check` · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` ·
file-size check (all `src/*.rs` < 1000 lines) · `cargo test --all-features`
(141 tests pass) · `cargo test --doc` · `cargo build --release`.

Version bump is intentionally **not** hand-edited in `Cargo.toml` — the repo
derives it from the `changelog.d` fragment (`bump: minor`), enforced by the
`prevent_manual_version_modification` policy.

## What this PR does

Implements multi-provider **subscription** support and API routing in the router
engine, adopting the best practices from
[heyhuynhgiabuu/proxypal](https://github.com/heyhuynhgiabuu/proxypal) /
[CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI), so the router can
"fully support claude, codex, gemini, qwen, and their subscriptions with all our
features and more."

Per the governing directive on this PR, this is implemented as a **CLI / Docker /
library engine with no UI**, on the **latest stable Rust** with **all
dependencies updated**.

## Engine changes

- **Multi-vendor OAuth credential reader** (`src/subscription.rs`) — reads each
  vendor CLI's credential file **read-only**: `~/.codex/auth.json`,
  `~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json`, `~/.qwen/oauth_creds.json` (Claude via the
  existing `~/.claude` reader). The router never writes to vendor locations.
- **Subscription routing** (`src/subscription_proxy.rs`, `src/gemini.rs`) — new
  `UpstreamProvider::{Codex, Gemini, Qwen}` upstreams route
  `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/models` to the correct
  vendor backend (ChatGPT Codex Responses API, Gemini Code Assist `generateContent`,
  DashScope OpenAI-compatible).
- **Dialect translation matrix** — OpenAI Chat Completions ↔ OpenAI Responses
  (Codex) ↔ Gemini Code Assist `generateContent`, including **SSE synthesis** when
  a client requests streaming from Gemini.
- **In-memory OAuth refresh** (`src/refresh.rs`) — expired Codex/Gemini/Qwen
  tokens are refreshed via each vendor's **public** OAuth client and cached **in
  memory only**; vendor files stay read-only and secrets are never logged. No
  OAuth client secret is hardcoded — Gemini's installed-app secret is supplied at
  runtime via the `GEMINI_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` env var.
- **`router doctor`** now probes each subscription credential file and reports
  present / token OK / EXPIRED / NO TOKEN / MISSING.
- **Rate-limit relay** — `Retry-After` and `x-ratelimit-*` headers from
  subscription upstreams are passed through so clients can back off intelligently.

## Dependencies & toolchain

- Updated all dependencies to latest and adopted **Rust edition 2024** on the
  latest stable toolchain (`build(deps): ...` commit).

## Case-study package

The evidence-backed analysis under
[`docs/case-studies/issue-37/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/tree/issue-37-69d3f0803294/docs/case-studies/issue-37)
collects the data, analyzes ProxyPal/CLIProxyAPI, lists every requirement
(`requirements.md`, F1–F12), proposes a plan per requirement
(`solution-plans.md`), and surveys components (`components-survey.md`). Online
research with cited primary sources and redacted secrets is in
`online-research.md`.

### Key finding

**ProxyPal is a UX shell, not an engine** — a Tauri/SolidJS GUI wrapping the Go
CLIProxyAPI binary. "Adopt the best of ProxyPal" therefore resolves to adopting
CLIProxyAPI's *engine* architecture (per-provider OAuth, dialect translation,
account rotation/cooldown) natively in our Rust engine — which this PR does — while
its GUI/auto-config UX is explicitly **out of scope** per the no-UI directive.

## Requirement status (functional, F1–F12)

| Done | Partial | Deferred / Out of scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F1 Claude, F2 Codex, F3 Gemini, F4 Qwen, F5 provider abstraction, F7 token refresh, F11 dialect matrix | F8 account pool (rate-limit relay + Claude pool), F10 quota observability (doctor) | F6 native login (delegated to vendor CLIs by design), F9 auto-config, F12 GUI (no-UI directive) |

Full trace in [`requirements.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-37-69d3f0803294/docs/case-studies/issue-37/requirements.md).

## Security

- Vendor credential files are read **read-only** — the router never writes
  `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini`, `~/.qwen`, `~/.claude`.
- Refresh tokens / access tokens / private keys are never logged.
- No OAuth client secret is committed to source — Gemini's is supplied via env var.
- `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; clippy all/pedantic/nursery clean.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` → 0 warnings.
- `cargo test` → 170 tests pass (111 lib + 49 integration + 10 release-tooling),
  including unit tests for the refresh layer, rate-limit header selection, and URL
  joining per provider.
- A `changelog.d/` fragment (`bump: minor`) documents the new capabilities.

Closes #37

## Summary

This PR delivers the research half of issue #9: a deep case study comparing this router against [diegosouzapw/OmniRoute](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute) and its lineage, framed as a concrete requirement inventory and phased solution plan that a follow-up implementation PR can pick up directly. No source code changes ship in this PR; the router runtime stays at v0.6.0 behaviour.

The single highest-leverage finding is that introducing a `Provider` trait is the load-bearing change. Every other issue-#9 requirement — Codex / Gemini / Qwen / OpenCode support, multi-subscription pools, cross-provider fallback, and the unified `la_sk_…` token across every front-door protocol — either depends on that trait or becomes much smaller once it exists.

Fixes #9 (research portion); the implementation slice is scoped in [requirements.md](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/blob/issue-9-d545a925a750/docs/case-studies/issue-9/requirements.md) Phases A-F (MUST/SHOULD) with Phases G-H (EXP) deferred to follow-up issues.

## What's in this PR

New documents under `docs/case-studies/issue-9/`:

- `README.md` — overview, key findings, recommended architecture, phased delivery plan, scope boundaries.
- `requirements.md` — 28-item requirement inventory (R1-R28) with MUST/SHOULD/EXP priorities, source-quote map back to the issue body, per-requirement solution plan in Phases A-H, existing components/libraries table, acceptance signals, and non-goals.
- `current-router-gap-analysis.md` — post-v0.6.0 capability assessment with `src/` evidence pointers and per-section gap tables (Provider model, Routing & resilience, API surface, Token surface, Operator surface, Compatibility/cost-control layers).
- `external-projects.md` — snapshot table + capability matrix + pattern-by-pattern reading for OmniRoute, 9router, CLIProxyAPI, musistudio/claude-code-router, LiteLLM, and Caveman.
- `online-research.md` — per-source research notes plus provider documentation cross-references for Anthropic, OpenAI/Codex, Google Gemini, Qwen, OpenCode, and OpenRouter.
- `raw/` — fetched README and metadata snapshots for each compared project (snapshot date 2026-05-03).

Changelog fragment:

- `changelog.d/20260503_140000_issue_9_case_study.md` (`bump: patch`) — the docs ship with the next release.

## Key recommendations (full detail in `docs/case-studies/issue-9/README.md`)

| Layer | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| Provider model | Introduce a `Provider` trait owning `auth + base URL + translate request + translate response + capabilities` |
| Account model | Generalise `MultiAccountRouter` to `MultiProviderRouter` keyed by `(provider, account)` pairs |
| OAuth | Per-provider OAuth refresher behind feature flags: Claude (existing) + Codex / Gemini / Qwen / Kiro / Qoder |
| Front-door routes | Add Gemini (`v1beta/models/<id>:generateContent` etc.) and Qwen DashScope alongside existing Anthropic and OpenAI surfaces |

| Routing engine | Four-tier fallback chain (Subscription → API → Cheap → Free) as ordered `(provider, model)` nodes in `.lenv` |
| Compression | `--compression=off|lite|standard|aggressive|ultra`, default `off`; only `lite` safe to auto-enable |

## Scope boundaries

In scope for the implementation PR that follows this case study (MUST/SHOULD, Phases A-F):

- `Provider` trait with at least Claude, Codex, Gemini, Qwen, OpenCode implementations behind feature flags
- multi-provider multi-account routing with the four-tier fallback chain
- Gemini and Qwen front-door routes alongside existing Anthropic / OpenAI surfaces
- unified `la_sk_…` token accepted on every front door, with scopes and per-token rate limits
- per-provider Prometheus counters and `/v1/usage` rows
- `provider` CLI subcommand
- `--compression=off|lite` only

Deferred to dedicated follow-up issues (EXP, Phases G partial / H):

- compression `standard / aggressive / ultra` (semantics-changing; needs benchmarks)
- MCP server, A2A protocol, agent card
- multi-modal APIs beyond chat / embeddings (images, video, music, TTS, STT, moderation, rerank, search, batch)

## Summary
Implements the full vision for issue #7: a single binary that supersedes the
features of every Claude MAX proxy in the comparison set, with conflicts
resolved via configuration toggles instead of forks.

Closes #7.

## What's new
- **Persistent token store** with text (Lino) + binary backends. Backend(s)
  selected via `--storage-policy` / `STORAGE_POLICY` (`memory`, `text`,
  `binary`, default `both`). Tokens, labels, expiries, revocations survive
  process restarts.
- **Multi-account routing** — `--additional-account-dirs` registers extra
  Claude MAX credential directories alongside the primary. The router picks
  a healthy account per request; on upstream 429 the failing account is
  parked on cooldown and the next one is used. Strategies: round-robin
  (default), priority, least-used.
- **OpenAI-compatible API surface** — `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`,
  `/v1/models`. Translates OpenAI request/response shapes to and from
  Anthropic Messages and maps `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `o1/o3/o4`, `gpt-5`
  to the equivalent Claude tier. Native `claude-*` IDs pass through.
- **Live observability** — Prometheus `/metrics`, JSON `/v1/usage`, and per-
  account health at `/v1/accounts`.
- **First-class CLI** built on `lino-arguments` (clap drop-in with `.lenv`
  support): `serve`, `tokens issue|list|revoke|expire|show`,
  `accounts list`, `doctor`. Token operations bypass the HTTP layer and
  share state with the server, so a token issued by `tokens issue` is
  immediately listable via the running server's admin endpoints.
- **Admin endpoints** (`/api/tokens/list`, `/api/tokens/revoke`) gated by
  the optional `--admin-key` / `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` Bearer.
- **Feature toggles** — `--disable-openai-api`, `--disable-anthropic-api`,
  `--disable-metrics`, `--experimental-compatibility`. Every API surface
  can be turned off without rebuilding.

## How to reproduce
1. `cargo run -- tokens issue --label demo` — issues a token, persists to
   `<data_dir>/tokens.{lino,bin}` and prints `la_sk_…` on stdout.
2. `cargo run -- tokens list` — shows the same token in a fresh process.
3. `cargo run` — starts the server. `/v1/chat/completions`,
   `/v1/responses`, `/v1/models` are live; `/metrics`, `/v1/usage`,
   `/v1/accounts` expose live counters.
4. Set `--additional-account-dirs path-a,path-b` to fan requests across
   accounts.

## Validation
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
  (pedantic + nursery enabled in `Cargo.toml`)
- `cargo test --all-features` — **44 unit + 39 integration = 83 tests passing**

## Test plan
- [x] OpenAI translation tests (model aliases, system+user folding,
      Anthropic→OpenAI response shape, `/v1/models` listing)
- [x] Prometheus rendering + `/v1/usage` JSON snapshot
- [x] CLI parser tests (default/serve/tokens issue/doctor/disable flags)
- [x] Token round-trip across persistent stores (memory/text/binary/both)
- [x] Multi-account router round-robin, priority, least-used + cooldowns
- [x] All previously existing routing/header/version tests still pass

## Notes
- `RoutingMode::Cli` and `RoutingMode::Hybrid` parse but currently log a
  warning and fall back to `Direct` — the local Claude CLI subprocess
  driver is the next slice (issue #7 R8/R9).
- Streaming SSE for OpenAI endpoints buffers and emits at end of stream;
  the translation primitives are unit-tested so per-chunk re-emission can
  be added without re-deriving the schema.
- Hand-rolled minimal Lino-style codec inside `src/storage.rs` until
  `lino-objects-codec` is published.
